Damage and Loss Model Library
  • Damage Models
  • California RC Bridges 2025 (Chen et al.): Components
  • CRCB - California RC bridges (Chen et al. 2025)
  • CRCB.E2 - Era 2 (1971–1990)
  • CRCB.E2.S3P - three or more spans
  • CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P - multi-column bents
  • CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S - seat abutments

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S - seat abutments

The following models are available:

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.AbAct.BoxGirder.MCB.Circ.M17 | Active abutment fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and seat abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, bents with three to five columns, circular columns.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 857 (spreadsheet row 859), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, AbAct; source note “Box-girder, circular column”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)


Mangalathu, S. 2017. Performance Based Grouping and Fragility Analysis of Box-Girder Bridges in California. PhD thesis, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA. https://hdl.handle.net/1853/58291.
Chen, S., Y. Xie, C. Wu, H. V. Burton, J. E. Padgett, and Á. Zsarnóczay. 2025. Second-generation component and system-level seismic fragility models for reinforced concrete bridges in California. Earthquake Spectra, 41 (4): 3234–3253. https://doi.org/10.1177/87552930251343634.

Model attributes: box-girder deck, two-column bents, three modeled spans, one-way flared columns with a 102 mm (4 in.) gap.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 860 (spreadsheet row 862), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, AbAct; source note “Box-girder, one-way flared column”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Jeon, Mangalathu, and Lee (2019), a study of California concrete box-girder bridges with flared two-column bents. The analyses use the Baker et al. (2011) PEER transportation suite scaled by a factor of two (320 motions). The authors state that the curves are valid only for the selected bridge classes: straight three-span Era 2 bridges with two-column bents. Flared columns: Flr1 is a one-way flared column with a 102 mm (4 in.) gap between the flare and the superstructure (BRIDGE-G of the study), Flr1T a one-way flared column along the transverse direction without a gap (BRIDGE-F1), and Flr2 a two-way flared column (BRIDGE-F2). The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.AbPass.BoxGirder.MCB.Circ.M17 | Passive abutment fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and seat abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, bents with three to five columns, circular columns.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 865 (spreadsheet row 867), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, AbPass; source note “Box-girder, circular column”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)

Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.Approach.Cant.Slope30.SXR22 | Approach settlement fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and seat abutments. Model attributes: cantilever abutment on spread footing, slope offset with a 30 ft approach slab.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 911 (spreadsheet row 913), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Approach; source note “Cantilever abutment on spread footing with approach slab damage through slope offset, with an approach slab length of 30 ft.”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods’ medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.
The source gives N/A for the moderate state, which the database uses to mark a negligible probability of that damage from ground shaking.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.Approach.Pile.Slope30.SXR22 | Approach settlement fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and seat abutments. Model attributes: abutment on piles, slope offset with a 30 ft approach slab.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 912 (spreadsheet row 914), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Approach; source note “Abutment on piles with approach slab (length 30 ft) damage through slope offset”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods’ medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.Bearing.BoxGirder.MCB.Circ.M17 | Bearing fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and seat abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, bents with three to five columns, circular columns.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 881 (spreadsheet row 883), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Bearing; source note “Box-girder, circular column”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 884 (spreadsheet row 886), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Bearing; source note “Box-girder, one-way flared column”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Jeon, Mangalathu, and Lee (2019), a study of California concrete box-girder bridges with flared two-column bents. The analyses use the Baker et al. (2011) PEER transportation suite scaled by a factor of two (320 motions). The authors state that the curves are valid only for the selected bridge classes: straight three-span Era 2 bridges with two-column bents. Flared columns: Flr1 is a one-way flared column with a 102 mm (4 in.) gap between the flare and the superstructure (BRIDGE-G of the study), Flr1T a one-way flared column along the transverse direction without a gap (BRIDGE-F1), and Flr2 a two-way flared column (BRIDGE-F2). The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.
The published parameters equal those of CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.Bearing.BoxGirder.TCB.Span3.Obl.JML19 at the two decimals of the source; Jeon, Mangalathu, and Lee (2019, Tables 4 and 5) give values for the two configurations that differ by less than that rounding.

Model attributes: box-girder deck, two-column bents, three modeled spans, one-way flared columns (transverse flare, no gap).

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 885 (spreadsheet row 887), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Bearing; source note “Box-girder, one-way flared column along the transverse direction”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Jeon, Mangalathu, and Lee (2019), a study of California concrete box-girder bridges with flared two-column bents. The analyses use the Baker et al. (2011) PEER transportation suite scaled by a factor of two (320 motions). The authors state that the curves are valid only for the selected bridge classes: straight three-span Era 2 bridges with two-column bents. Flared columns: Flr1 is a one-way flared column with a 102 mm (4 in.) gap between the flare and the superstructure (BRIDGE-G of the study), Flr1T a one-way flared column along the transverse direction without a gap (BRIDGE-F1), and Flr2 a two-way flared column (BRIDGE-F2). The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.Column.BoxGirder.MCB.Circ.M17 | Column fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and seat abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, bents with three to five columns, circular columns.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 841 (spreadsheet row 843), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Column; source note “Box-girder, circular column”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 850 (spreadsheet row 852), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Unseating; source note “Box-girder, oblong column”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.Unseating.BoxGirder.TCB.Span3.Flr1.JML19 | Span unseating fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and seat abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, two-column bents, three modeled spans, one-way flared columns with a 102 mm (4 in.) gap.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 852 (spreadsheet row 854), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Unseating; source note “Box-girder, one-way flared column”. The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.
Source study: Jeon, Mangalathu, and Lee (2019), a study of California concrete box-girder bridges with flared two-column bents. The analyses use the Baker et al. (2011) PEER transportation suite scaled by a factor of two (320 motions). The authors state that the curves are valid only for the selected bridge classes: straight three-span Era 2 bridges with two-column bents. Flared columns: Flr1 is a one-way flared column with a 102 mm (4 in.) gap between the flare and the superstructure (BRIDGE-G of the study), Flr1T a one-way flared column along the transverse direction without a gap (BRIDGE-F1), and Flr2 a two-way flared column (BRIDGE-F2). The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.
The source defines unseating capacity for extensive and complete only. The slight and moderate limit states are set equal to the extensive limit state so that pelicun can evaluate the model; those two states cannot occur.

Suggested Block Size: 1 EA (round up to integer quantity)
